physical.medium_raw: Printed, tie-and dye, and wax-resist dyed cotton
physical.physical_description:
Man's headdress of printed, tie-and dye, and wax-resist dyed (Batik) cotton. The centre is dyed green by the tie-and-dye (kain kembangan) process. The remainder of the field and the inner and outer borders are obtained by the Batik method. The pattern is printed from hand-stamps covered with hot wax and dyed blue and brown on a buff-coloured ground.

In the centre is a green square 'modang' with buff-coloured edges on which is a pattern in-turned hooks and bands of small repeated geometrical motives. The field around this is of dark blue. The wide outer border is printed with a design of moths alternating with cross-formed floral scrolls amid a diaper of hooks. Inside, projecting into the blue field, is a row of round-headed panels each charged with a hook and from which slopes a wavy line.

cultural.vision_reason: This is a hand-drawn batik and tie-dye (tritik) cotton selendang (shoulder cloth) from Surakarta, a classic Javanese textile made and worn as women's dress in Central Java.

physical.physical_description: Woman's shawl (Selendang) of tie-and-dyed and wax-resist dyed cotton. The centre (modang) is dyed blue by the tie-and-dye (kain kembangan) process, and the borders are of Batik-work, the design being drawn by hand and dyed by the wax resist method in brown and blue. The centre is in grey-blue. The border has a wide band of diamond-shaped compartments each enclosing a floral form and narrower fillets of geometrical and floral motives. Outside the central field is a crackle network with spikes carried into the central field.
